content:
Hi all, my name is Rob Sneiderman, and this my first contribution of Ville inequality for mathlib4. I opened PR #40085, adding Ville’s inequality for nonnegative supermartingales.
The CI is green and it is now ready for review.
I am new to the mathlib review process and will keep technical discussion on the PR unless reviewers prefer Zulip. Thank you all!
@Robert Sneiderman, unfortunately, per new Mathlib policy, we currently don't accept PRs from the new contributors that make significant use of AI.

(I think this PR is pretty decent, but those are the rules we decided on :woman_shrugging:. It's essential, given that we have very little reviewer bandwidth, that we know a human is learning from the review process. The intent of the policy is that you make some initial human only PRs, to learn the process, and then are able to make PRs with AI assistance after that,.)

It may also be mentioned that upstreaming work for #Brownian motion , will likely have more generally indexed results for sub/super martingale inequalities ( I believe there is also a more direct way to do this currently than this PR , using the sub-martingale results in a slicker way).

@Kim Morrison Thank you Kim. Thank you for clarifying.

I want to add some context: I use AI tools as an accessibility aid, including because of related limitations. I am not trying to bypass mathematical review or use maintainers as validators for work I do not understand. My intent was to contribute a correct formalization, learn the mathlib process, and receive ordinary technical feedback.

I understand reviewer bandwidth is limited, and I respect that maintainers need policies to manage the queue. At the same time, I would appreciate clarification on how the policy applies when AI is being used as an accessibility tool rather than as a replacement for contributor responsibility.

Could someone point me to the specific policy defining “significant use of AI,” and whether there is a path for contributors who use AI assistively to still participate, perhaps with smaller PRs or additional explanation of the human review performed before submission?

I am happy to follow a reasonable onboarding path, but I would like to understand the expectations clearly.

thank you for your consideration,
Rob
Can you explain what "using AI tools as an accessibility aid" entails, exactly, in this context? Sorry for my ignorance on this matter.

@Jireh Loreaux thank you for the question. I use AI in part as an accessibility aid. I'd prefer not to discuss personal details publicly, but the tools help me navigate Lean, library discovery, error messages, proof development, and related tasks more effectively.

Regardless of the tools used, I remain responsible for understanding, validating, and submitting the final work. And this includes the final writing of all my posts and work, including these posts and messages here.
Rob

Accessibility aside , though it’s hard to gather what it means , why do you specifically want to contribute this content to Mathlib?

There are other repos that are more accessible to AI, but Mathlib especially seeks insight and understanding of the best way to formalise something , rather than simply correct statements that work.

@Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 Thank you for the question.

I wanted to put it in mathlib because Ville’s inequality is a standard martingale result, so I thought it could belong in the shared probability library rather than just in my own repo if it were to be received.

I understand your point, thank you for the information.

I am trying to learn the right way to formalize these martingale inequalities so they are useful in mathlib long term.

Rob
Your PR looks very reasonable. Can you pick one of the AI contribution scales going around on blogs and forums and locate your PR on it?

The reason why we disallow AI contributions from new contributors is because we don't trust that the new contributor will do anything more with the feedback than passing it onto their LLM and back. It doesn't seem like you would be doing so, therefore I am happy to review your PR.

@Yaël Dillies Thank you for the comment.

My workflow is: I study relevant math/probability background myself, including from physical textbooks, and then I use AI to help with literature search, mathlib search, looking through existing PRs, understanding the Lean structure, and checking whether the project was feasible before attempting it.

I use Whispr for voice control and Claude Code to help with literature review, repo-history search, and summarizing the existing topics (in this case martingales in mathlib). I understand the intended theorem statement, the optional-stopping/hitting-time proof idea, and why Ville’s inequality belongs near the existing martingale/maximal-inequality infrastructure. I am not using ai tools like openclaw/clawdbot for example.

Thank you for your consideration,
Rob

Let's pick the scale at https://www.visidata.org/blog/2026/ai/#self-assessed-ai-level-for-contributions, as an example. Where would you place your level of AI use (ignoring the speech to text conversion here is fine)?

@Michael Rothgang thank you for the link. After looking at it I would say my work on this pr was between the number 5 and the number 6 on that list. I say maybe 6 because I could be mistaken in my final understanding as I am not an expert.
Thanks
Rob
